solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Native American turned up, working round island

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards, so backwards
the word for working is placed around the island's name

parts.note: a machine that is working is on
Java is an island of Indonesia

explanation.surface: Someone of Native American heritage has come back and is busy around an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses the whole thing, as befits a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Navajo are a Native American people of the south-western United States.

clue.text: Complex officer getting over very good luck

parts.note: a maze is a complex network of paths
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an officer
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: An officer gets past a complicated system with outstanding fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: Mazel tov is a Yiddish/Hebrew expression of congratulation, literally wishing someone good fortune.

clue.text: Porsche finally stopping old car design

indicators.note: a letter stopping a word plugs a gap inside it, so it goes within

parts.note: crate is slang for a battered old car

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of Porsche

explanation.surface: A Porsche brought to a halt by a clapped-out vintage vehicle, in some motoring design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes E, the end of Porsche, which 'stopping' places inside CRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To design something is to invent or make it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Note sent round unknown university before a dance

indicators.note: the enclosed group comes ahead of the letter a
the word for note is wrapped around the next two letters

parts.note: to mark something is to note it
z is a mathematical unknown, like x and y

explanation.surface: A memo circulated about an unnamed university ahead of a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent round' puts Z and U inside MARK, and A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The mazurka is a lively Polish folk dance in triple time.

clue.text: Entire football team extremely excited to be included

indicators.note: the outer letters are to go inside the team's name

parts.note: United is a common name for a football team, such as Manchester United

indicators.note: extremely takes the extreme letters, first and last, of excited

explanation.surface: A whole football team gets thoroughly worked up and joins in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entire' looks like it describes the team, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Text left unedited is complete, with nothing cut, so it is whole.

clue.text: Medal possibly trendy for king of literature

parts.note: the OBE (Officer of the Order of the British Empire) is a British honour, loosely a medal
R ON stands for 'right on', slang for fashionably progressive

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a fashionable decoration suits a literary monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trendy' is RON, read as R ON, short for right-on.
explanation.definitionFit: Oberon is king of the fairies in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: Dismal exhibit behind rare event

parts.note: blue means sad or gloomy
to moon is to show one's bare bottom as a prank

explanation.surface: A gloomy display trailing behind something that seldom happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exhibit behind' reads as 'display at the back', but it means baring one's backside.
explanation.definitionFit: Once in a blue moon is an idiom for something happening very seldom.

clue.text: Article in Le Monde dividing chaotic Arabic region

indicators.note: the article splits the scrambled letters in two by sitting among them
chaotic letters are disordered, so they are rearranged

parts.note: la is the French feminine definite article, as a Le Monde writer would use

explanation.surface: A French newspaper piece splits opinion on some disorderly Arabic text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chaotic' rearranges the letters into CABRIA before 'dividing' places the article inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Calabria is a region of southern Italy, forming the toe of the boot.

clue.text: Extra VIP going ahead of everybody

indicators.note: the important person comes first, in front of the word for everybody

parts.note: a nob is a wealthy or important person
all means everybody

explanation.surface: An additional bigwig pushes in front of the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a no-ball is an illegal delivery, and the run awarded for it counts as an extra to the batting side.

clue.text: Country beginning to accept former labour leader

parts.note: Wales is a country of the United Kingdom

indicators.note: beginning to takes the opening letter of accept

explanation.surface: A nation starts to embrace an ex-Labour Party chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'labour' suggests the British Labour Party, but it is organised labour: Lech Walesa led the Polish union Solidarity.
explanation.definitionFit: Lech Walesa headed the Solidarity trade union before becoming Polish president.

clue.text: Trained end user with a submarine

indicators.note: trained letters are drilled into a new formation, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A consumer who has been coached is given a submarine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trained' reorders END USER into UNDERSE, followed by A.
explanation.definitionFit: Submarine as an adjective means lying or operating beneath the sea's surface.

clue.text: Hold below this scarf, taking time to dress

indicators.note: the scarf takes on the time letter immediately after it

parts.note: a boa is a long fluffy scarf
to deck is to dress or adorn

explanation.surface: Store this below while a scarf takes ages to put on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold' is the ship's cargo space, not a grip.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship the cargo hold lies beneath the upper deck where lifeboats are carried.

clue.text: Inferior cast accepting rejected work

indicators.note: the word for cast takes the other piece into its middle

parts.note: a cast is a tint or tinge of colour

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A poor-quality acting troupe takes on a play that was turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' suggests actors, but it is a tinge of colour; 'rejected' gives PO.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinpot describes something shoddy or second-rate, especially a petty regime.

clue.text: Saw book by good mathematician?

indicators.note: by means beside, so the letter for book sits next to the mathematician

parts.note: a good mathematician proves things, so is a prover

explanation.surface: Someone saw a book written by a gifted mathematician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a verb but is the noun, an old saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is a traditional saying or maxim, the same as an adage.

clue.text: Company cutting almost all wealth needing time to bounce back

indicators.note: the result needs the time letter added at the end
the company abbreviation cuts into the shortened word, splitting it
almost all means dropping the final letter

parts.note: riches means wealth

explanation.surface: A firm slashing nearly all its assets needs time to recover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost all' leaves RICHE, which the company abbreviation splits; 'needing' adds the time letter at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To ricochet is to rebound off a surface, as a bullet or stone does.

clue.text: What might confuse AA seller?

indicators.note: the phrase names whatever would scramble the following letters, so it signals rearranging them

explanation.surface: Someone asks what would perplex a seller of something to do with the AA.
explanation.walkthrough: AA here is Alcoholics Anonymous; strong beer is just what would befuddle one of its members, so the whole clue is also the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Real ales are traditional cask-conditioned beers, intoxicating drinks that befuddle.

clue.text: Set by 80s post-punk musician

definitions.meaning: set means determined, fixed in one's purpose
... was the frontman of Adam and the Ants, an early-1980s British new-wave band

explanation.surface: Someone is accompanied by a 1980s post-punk performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being set on something means being unyielding and determined, unshakeably resolved.

clue.text: Wife born in America almost changed character

indicators.note: the two abbreviations are placed within the shortened country
changed signals that the letters are altered in order
almost means the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A wife born in the USA became almost unrecognisable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts AMERICA to AMERIC; 'in' adds W and B, and 'changed' rearranges the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilkins Micawber is the ever-hopeful debtor in Dickens's David Copperfield, a fictional figure.

clue.text: Traveller's type of knife

definitions.meaning: Henry Morton ... was the explorer who found Livingstone in Africa
a ... knife is a retractable-blade utility knife, a British brand name

explanation.surface: A wayfarer's kind of blade.
explanation.definitionFit: The explorer H. M. Stanley shares his surname with the Stanley utility-knife brand.

clue.text: Monster, in seconds, caught friend from behind

parts.note: c is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: read from behind means taking the letters back to front

parts.note: an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A beast catches a companion from the rear in a matter of seconds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from behind' reverses ALLY to YLLA.
explanation.definitionFit: Scylla is the many-headed sea creature of Greek myth facing Charybdis across a strait.

clue.text: Snooty boy and girl

parts.note: a lad is a boy
Ida is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A haughty young man and woman.
explanation.definitionFit: La-di-da mocks affected, pretentious manners, the speech of someone stuck-up.

clue.text: Former number one in the chart following remix

indicators.note: a remix reworks a recording, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A one-time chart-topper back in the hit parade after a remix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number one' suggests a hit record, but it means the Prime Minister: Margaret Thatcher, PM 1979-90.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret Thatcher was British Prime Minister, the country's top political figure, in the 1980s.

clue.text: Lawsuit in France taken out of proportion

indicators.note: the country abbreviation is removed from the longer word

parts.note: a fraction is a proportion or part

explanation.surface: A legal case in France is blown out of all proportion.
explanation.definitionFit: An action is a legal proceeding brought in court, a suit.

clue.text: Obtain delight when naked

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its outer covering, so first and last letters go

parts.note: felicity means great happiness or delight

explanation.surface: Getting pleasure from going without clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To elicit is to draw out or extract, as a reply, so to get it.

clue.text: Announced check on drug problem for the environment?

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the second part follows the drug

parts.note: acid is slang for LSD

indicators.note: announced means spoken, so the word for check is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to rein is to check or restrain

explanation.surface: A drug test is publicly declared to be an environmental issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Announced' gives REIN as it sounds, RAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid rain, polluted with sulphur and nitrogen oxides, damages forests and lakes.

clue.text: Keep stopping to oblige non- student

indicators.note: the word for keep plugs the gap inside, stopping it up

parts.note: to tie someone is to oblige or bind them
to own something is to keep it

explanation.surface: Holding things up to do someone a favour, as an outsider at a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep stopping' reads as 'keep halting', but the possession word goes into TIE.
explanation.definitionFit: In university towns a resident who is not a student is called a townie, in contrast to gown.

clue.text: Half of unnecessary workers maybe cut as a necessity

indicators.note: half of takes the first four of the eight letters

parts.note: needless means unnecessary

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the final letters are dropped

parts.note: worker bees are the workers of a hive, so bees are an example of workers

explanation.surface: Half the redundant staff may have to be let go if required.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half of' gives NEED from NEEDLESS; 'cut' docks BEES to BE.
explanation.definitionFit: Need be, as in 'if need be', means if it is required: when necessary.

clue.text: Mysterious sea-scouts regularly spotted west of Morecambe

indicators.note: in an across entry, west of means to the left, so before
regularly spotted means every other letter is picked out

parts.note: Eric Morecambe was a much-loved British comedian, of Morecambe and Wise

explanation.surface: Odd sea scouts are seen at regular intervals off the Lancashire coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly spotted' gives ESOT; Morecambe is a Lancashire resort, but here the comedian Eric Morecambe, whose first name comes before his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric means understood only by an inner few, so obscure or mysterious.
